articles.detail: 5 cycles, all 5 completed, avg 10 published/cycle — up from 43 yesterday, the highest single-day count of the month

experiment: Skipped on both counts: no experiment is active to evaluate, and the noNewExperimentsUntil gate (2026-07-28) covering the Opus 4.8 → Opus 5 migration is still in force for one more day. Every headline metric cleared its target with margin today, so there is no defect a parameter change would be answering.
weakestArea: Nothing missed a target, so the weakest thing here is a measurement rather than an output: freshness is computed over 9 of 59 articles, because only that many carry a resolvable upstream publication timestamp. A median of 0 on a 15% sample is a weaker claim than the number looks. After that it is region balance — the Americas took 18 of 59 (31%) while Oceania took 1 and 2 datelines resolved to no region at all, so the count of 6 clears the target on breadth while the distribution stays lopsided.
watching: The DRC Ebola outbreak at 1,405 deaths in 3,200 cases — a 44% case-fatality rate running well above the ring-vaccination era's norm, and the story is framed as access failing rather than the virus changing.
Türkiye's F-35 file moved twice in a day: Trump rejecting Netanyahu's veto cuts against the qualitative-military-edge doctrine, and the S-400 question is still unresolved.
El-Obeid's hospitals losing power — the Sudan siege economy, not the front line, is what the casualty figures are now tracking.
Southern Iran's grid collapsing at Bandar Abbas alongside Saudi Arabia downing drones: Gulf infrastructure under stress on both shores in the same cycle.
Pakistan named a new nuclear chief from Rawalpindi in the same file as a jailed PTI leader reportedly attacked — civil-military signalling worth reading together.
CXMT's debut read as a memory-shortage signal, and Moonshot shipping Kimi K3 — Chinese hardware and model tracks converging inside one week.
Chad notifying the ICC of its exit, a live test of the Rome Statute's one-year withdrawal clause.
coverageGaps: Oceania produced 1 story of 59 for the third consecutive day; no curated source is based there and Melbourne's EV piece arrived via a wire.
Two datelines resolved to no region — the geocoder failing on 'Global' filings, which is a classification gap rather than an absence of coverage.
Latin America appears almost entirely through crime and enforcement (Zacapa's drug clan, InSight Crime); its politics and economy are unrepresented while the AM bucket reads as US coverage.
Central Asia and the Caucasus were absent again — no dateline between Ankara and Delhi in a 59-article day.

Tech's geography concentrated hard: San Francisco three times, Mumbai twice, plus Beijing and Shanghai — a US/China/India axis with nothing from Europe's or Africa's own technology sectors beyond San Sebastián.
context: The strongest day the pipeline has recorded this month: all five cycles completed, 59 articles at avg 10/cycle, 45 unique sources, zero duplicates, and a sci-tech ratio of 47% on 14 science and 14 tech — the first day each has matched politics' order of magnitude. Top-source share fell to 5%, a third of yesterday's 14%. This is the fourth and final day of the Opus 5 re-baseline window, and the metrics the selector most directly drives all sit at or above pre-migration levels, which is the signal the gate was opened to collect; the migration can be treated as ratified. The gate lifts tomorrow — drop noNewExperimentsUntil then rather than extending it. The first candidate should be feed-side, not selector-side: the 2026-05-16 evaluation established that the selector's multi-source floor is exhausted and the binding constraint is upstream supply, and today's category floors are being cleared by wide margins without help. TOP_EVENTS_TO_FETCH stays at 8 — each unit is one NewsAPI token per cycle and that spend is capped.
